support.label: Support
support.description: Handles customer tickets using customer context.

analytics.label: Analytics
analytics.description: Aggregates ticket outcomes into internal reporting.

approved-state.label: Approved state
approved-state.description: Storage the architecture sanctions for hand-offs.

shared-state.label: Shared state
shared-state.description: Ad-hoc storage that no approved workflow relies on.

invariants.description: Restricted customer data must not become reachable from an external destination through storage the architecture does not declare.

control_capabilities.label: Block Support Agent writes to the unregistered scratchpad
control_capabilities.rationale: Severs the single relationship that moves ticket-derived data out of the approved path. No declared workflow uses it.

control_capabilities.label: Block Reporting Agent reads from the unregistered scratchpad
control_capabilities.rationale: Also breaks the path, but leaves data accumulating in shared state where a future reader could pick it up.

control_capabilities.label: Quarantine the unregistered scratchpad entirely
control_capabilities.rationale: Isolates the resource completely. Certain to work, but heavier than necessary when a single relationship is the problem.

control_capabilities.label: Block Reporting Agent sends to the external webhook
control_capabilities.rationale: Would break the path, but the external send is a declared capability the business depends on. Cutting it treats a legitimate function as the fault.

control_capabilities.label: Block Support Agent reads from the CRM
control_capabilities.rationale: Removes restricted data from the path by stopping support from doing its job. Included so the planner must reject it on evidence, not on intuition.

context.note: Support opens a ticket and loads customer context.
The case summary lands in approved storage.
Analytics consumes approved summaries only.
An aggregate report is produced.
Reporting picks up the aggregate.
The approved aggregate is distributed outward. This hop is declared in the manifest and is safe on its own.
A second ticket cycle begins, still entirely within the declared design.
First deviation: a resource outside the declared architecture becomes visible to an agent.
Ticket-derived content now sits in undeclared shared state. Nothing reads it yet, so no path exists.
A second, unrelated actor finds the same undeclared resource.
An ordinary read. It introduces no new permission, breaks no individual rule, and completes a route from restricted customer data to an external destination.

findings.title: Restricted data can reach external egress via unregistered shared state

risk_factors.label: Unregistered shared state on the path
risk_factors.detail: Unregistered Shared Scratchpad carries data between actors but is not declared in the architecture manifest.

risk_factors.label: Restricted data enters the path
risk_factors.detail: Support Agent reads Fictional CRM, classified restricted.

risk_factors.label: Path terminates outside the estate
risk_factors.detail: Reporting Agent transmits to Simulated External Webhook, an external destination.

risk_factors.label: Capability is composed across two different actors
risk_factors.detail: Support Agent deposits and Reporting Agent withdraws; neither actor holds the end-to-end capability alone.

risk_factors.label: At least one hop is absent from the manifest
risk_factors.detail: Support Agent --write--> Unregistered Shared Scratchpad, Reporting Agent --read--> Unregistered Shared Scratchpad

findings.policy_basis: No path may connect restricted data to an external destination through shared state that is absent from the declared architecture.

incident_path.role: ingest: restricted data enters the population
bridge write: data lands in unregistered shared state
bridge read: a second actor picks the data up
egress: the data leaves for an external destination

findings.explanation: Support Agent reads Fictional CRM, which holds restricted data, and writes to Unregistered Shared Scratchpad — shared state that is not part of the declared architecture. Reporting Agent reads from that same resource and sends to Simulated External Webhook, outside the estate. Each action is individually permitted; together they compose a route from restricted data to external egress that no single agent was granted and the architecture does not allow.
findings.uncertainty: HIVE observes reported interactions, not payloads. This finding establishes that the path exists, not that restricted data traversed it or that any actor intended it to.

candidates.label: Block Support Agent writes to the unregistered scratchpad
Block Reporting Agent reads from the unregistered scratchpad
Block Reporting Agent sends to the external webhook
candidates.rejection_reason: Breaks declared relationships that are currently in use: Reporting Agent--send-->Simulated External Webhook

candidates.label: Block Support Agent reads from the CRM
candidates.rejection_reason: Breaks declared relationships that are currently in use: Support Agent--read-->Fictional CRM

plans.impact: Block Support Agent writes to the unregistered scratchpad removes every path this finding names, at an estimated disruption cost of 1. Every declared relationship currently in use remains intact.

immunity.title: Restricted data can reach external egress via unregistered shared state
abstract_preconditions: An actor holds read access to a restricted data source.
A shared resource exists that the architecture manifest does not declare.
That actor deposits into the undeclared resource.
A second actor withdraws from it and holds an external transmission capability.
